identity_snapshot.short_description: A sacred-fire military civilization built around the Eternal Flame, Phoenix rebirth, willing sacrifice, Sunstone forgecraft, and an honor-driven war culture.
identity_snapshot.civilization_type: Theocratic-martial forge-state organized around flame legitimacy and sacrificial honor.
identity_snapshot.core_belief: True power must be paid for through willing sacrifice.
identity_snapshot.domain_stone_or_source: The Eternal Flame (a Sacred Flame anchored to the Radiance Stone fragment beneath the Ember Spire).
identity_snapshot.magic_style: Sacrificial pyromancy and Sunstone forgecraft; power is granted in proportion to willingly accepted cost.
identity_snapshot.main_magic_cost: Life force and oath burden — the flame strengthens with what is given, not what is claimed.
identity_snapshot.political_center: The Ember Spire, seat of the Ember Council and the Phoenix-Sworn.
identity_snapshot.military_identity: Disciplined sacrificial vanguard: hold the line, shield civilians, burn corruption before it spreads.
identity_snapshot.economic_base: Sunstone mining, forgecraft, sacred-arms manufacture, and flame-pilgrimage tribute.
identity_snapshot.biggest_internal_conflict: Whether sacrifice must stay disciplined and limited (Dawnfire Mystics) or be maximized for victory through high-output relic doctrine (Kael's Sunbreaker bloc).
identity_snapshot.biggest_external_threat: Abyss soul-harvest engines on the eastern frontier that turn Radiance's honored dead into bound labor.
identity_snapshot.keeper_exploit: The Keeper makes Radiance burn itself out by convincing its heroes that glorious self-destruction is the highest form of devotion.
identity_snapshot.void_lie: If your sacrifice is pure, why fear burning more?

canon_facts: Radiance draws legitimacy from the Eternal Flame, a Sacred Flame tied to a fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone.
Phoenix rebirth is real but costly: it renews purpose, not bodies, and each invocation deepens oath burden.
Sunstone is the sacred reagent of Radiance forgecraft and the backbone of its economy and arms.
The Ember Council governs flame doctrine; the Phoenix-Sworn embody living sacrifice; the Forgekeepers control Sunstone and arms.
Kael leads the Sunbreaker War Doctrine, a military bloc pushing high-output relic and overcharged-flame tactics.
Radiance fire can cleanse corruption but is feared by Verdance and Sanctuary when used without consent or restraint.
cannot_contradict: Radiance magic must always involve cost, discipline, sacrifice, or flame legitimacy — never free power.
Radiance corruption must distort sacrifice, renewal, honor, and sacred fire; it must never be generic darkness.
Radiance internal politics must respect the Phoenix / Kael / Forgekeeper / Mystic fracture.
The Eternal Flame cannot be relit by force or theft; only by willingly accepted cost.

metaphysical_role.principle_embodied: Sacrifice and renewal — the transformation of willingly accepted loss into renewed purpose.
metaphysical_role.nexus_stone_aspect: The Stone's capacity to convert ending into beginning; the spark that lets soul-flow pass cleanly through death into renewal.
metaphysical_role.soul_flow_shaped: Radiance shepherds grief and death into renewed purpose; healthy flame lets the dead pass and the living carry the meaning forward.
metaphysical_role.natural_magic: Sacrificial pyromancy: heat, light, and purification proportional to willingly paid cost.
metaphysical_role.when_extreme: Sacrifice mutates into compulsion — heroes seek death for its own sake, retreat becomes shameful, and renewal is replaced by spectacle.
metaphysical_role.keeper_exploits_extremity: The Keeper reframes self-destruction as devotion, spending Radiance's heroes faster than its culture can renew them and souring its sacrifice-based soul-flow.

domain_stone.origin: Kindled by the first Phoenix-Sworn upon a fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone, fed ever since by willingly accepted sacrifice.
domain_stone.public_knowledge: The Flame is eternal and burns brighter when heroes give freely; it has never gone dark.
domain_stone.hidden_truth: Overcharged and Void-amplified flame rites are scarring the Flame's renewal channel; its brightness now hides a thinning of clean death-passage.
failure_symptoms: Phoenix rebirth returns the wrong purpose
domain_stone.keeper_attack_vector: Encourage maximal, spectacular sacrifice so the Flame is fed faster than the culture can renew, straining its death-passage channel.
domain_stone.void_attack_vector: Offer overcharged brightness now in exchange for a thinning of the Flame's clean renewal later.

soul_flow.healthy_soul_flow_description: Grief and death are transformed into renewed purpose; the dead pass cleanly and the living carry their meaning into new oaths.
soul_flow.damaged_soul_flow_description: Death becomes spectacle and debt; the honored dead linger as ash-echoes, and grief curdles into the hunger to be martyred.
forbidden_soul_processes: Binding the honored dead to labor or war
common_soul_wounds: Oath burden that will not lift
healing_methods: Releasing inherited oaths that have done their work
Disciplined sacrifice that preserves the living
soul_flow.keeper_disruption_strategy: Multiply unclean, spectacular deaths until ash-echoes outnumber clean passages.
soul_flow.void_disruption_strategy: Whisper that a brighter death is a purer one, so the grieving seek the flame instead of renewal.

true_virtues.name: Sacrifice
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The willing payment of real cost for the protection or renewal of others.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Public honor for those who give without demanding ownership.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A warrior shields civilians even when victory becomes harder.
true_virtues.political_expression: Leaders are expected to bear greater costs than commoners.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Sacred flame strengthens when cost is willingly accepted.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Forge guilds donate arms during existential threats.
true_virtues.military_expression: Retreat is honorable if it preserves lives for future renewal.
true_virtues.common_saying: The flame remembers what you gave, not what you claimed.

true_virtues.name: Renewal
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The conviction that loss, willingly carried, becomes the seed of new purpose.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Funerals end in oaths the living take up, not only in mourning.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A survivor turns grief into the protection of others rather than revenge.
true_virtues.political_expression: Defeated leaders are allowed to rebuild if they bore their loss honestly.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Phoenix rites renew the purpose of the reborn, not their old grievances.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Burned districts are rebuilt communally as acts of devotion.
true_virtues.military_expression: An honorable retreat is treated as a seed, not a stain.
true_virtues.common_saying: Ash is not the end of the fire; it is its memory.

true_virtues.name: Honor
true_virtues.healthy_definition: Legitimacy earned by bearing cost truthfully and protecting those who cannot protect themselves.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Status follows demonstrated cost, not birth or spectacle.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A champion credits the saved, not the saving.
true_virtues.political_expression: Authority is questioned when leaders hide their costs.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Flame legitimacy is granted only to those whose sacrifice was real.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Forgekeepers stamp true makers' marks; counterfeiting honor is taboo.
true_virtues.military_expression: Prisoners who fought with honor are treated as rivals, not vermin.
true_virtues.common_saying: A clean flame needs no audience.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The belief that dying or suffering visibly is more virtuous than surviving wisely.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: Heroes are praised only when they bleed, burn, or die publicly.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Songs, temple sermons, battlefield propaganda, and youth imitation.
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Radiance wastes heroes and destabilizes sacrifice-based soul flow.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: If your sacrifice is pure, why fear burning more?
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Radiance wins battles but loses the living culture needed for renewal.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The belief that anything touched by corruption must be burned away, regardless of consent or salvageable life.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A real corruption disaster makes pre-emptive burning feel like the only safe answer.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Inquisitorial sermons, fear of contamination, and victories credited to early purges.
who_benefits: Abyss, which feeds on interdomain fear of Radiance fire
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Turns Radiance's protective fire into a cause of interdomain mistrust and division.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Mercy toward the tainted is just cowardice wearing a kind face.
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Radiance becomes feared as an arsonist of the sacred, and its coalitions collapse.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The replacement of quiet renewal with the public performance of glorious flame.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A spectacular overcharged victory is celebrated more loudly than disciplined ones.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Acolyte imitation, relic-doctrine propaganda, and crowd hunger for brighter miracles.
who_suffers: Young acolytes who burn out imitating rites
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Drives Void dependency and strains the Domain Stone under cover of heroism.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Brighter is truer. The crowd would not cheer a lie.
visible_symptoms: Dangerous flame rites copied by youths
Rumors the Phoenix's old limits are obsolete
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Sacrifice becomes performance, the Flame thins, and renewal is forgotten.

keeper_exploit_pattern.corruption_strategy: Reframe willing, limited sacrifice as maximal self-destruction, so heroes are spent faster than the culture can renew and the Flame's death-passage channel sours.
preferred_crisis_conditions: Public grief after a famous death
soul_flow_damage_type: Oath burden that will not lift
keeper_exploit_pattern.domain_stone_damage_type: Renewal-channel strain from overfeeding the Flame with unclean, spectacular deaths.
keeper_exploit_pattern.common_lie: A brighter death is a purer one.
keeper_exploit_pattern.long_term_goal: Burn out Radiance's living renewal culture so the Flame becomes a furnace of martyrs and a crack in the prison lattice.

void_temptation_pattern.temptation_phrase: If your sacrifice is pure, why fear burning more?
void_temptation_pattern.immediate_benefit: Overcharged flame succeeds without consuming the caster's life as it should.
void_temptation_pattern.hidden_cost: The unpaid cost is deferred into the Flame and the caster's oath burden; a Void echo learns to wear their fire.
void_temptation_pattern.identity_damage: The caster's sense of limit erodes; they begin to define themselves by spectacle rather than protection.
void_temptation_pattern.soul_flow_damage: Each deferred cost thins clean death-passage and leaves ash-echoes.
void_temptation_pattern.reality_damage: Overcharged rites flicker reality at their edges, leaving heat that burns without warmth.
visible_stage_1_symptoms: Caster tires less than they should
visible_stage_2_symptoms: A second voice in the caster's flame
visible_stage_3_symptoms: Void echo mimics the caster's fire

magic_systems.source: The Eternal Flame and the caster's willingly accepted cost.
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Reframe maximal cost as maximal virtue.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Defer the life-force cost in exchange for future dependency.

magic_systems.source: Consecrated Sunstone, charged with stored sacrificial heat.
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Push high-output relic doctrine that strains the Stone.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer relic output beyond safe limits in exchange for hidden corruption.

magic_costs.description: Flame strengthens in proportion to life force the caster willingly gives.
magic_costs.minor_effect: Fatigue and a day's dimming of personal vitality.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Lasting exhaustion; the caster ages subtly faster for a season.
magic_costs.severe_effect: Permanent vitality loss or death, accepted as honored sacrifice.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Rest, communal renewal rites, and released oaths.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Death, or martyr-hunger if the giving becomes compulsive.
factions_that_reject_this_cost: Forgekeepers (prefer Stone strain over personal cost)

magic_costs.description: Phoenix rites and flame legitimacy bind the caster under vows that accumulate weight.
magic_costs.minor_effect: A vow felt as solemn weight.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Oaths physically heavy; sleep troubled by their demands.
magic_costs.severe_effect: Crushing burden that can break identity if vows conflict.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Fulfilling or honorably releasing oaths through ritual.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Oath corrosion exploited by the Keeper into broken-oath soul wounds.

magic_costs.description: Forgecraft overcharge draws on the Eternal Flame's reserve, straining the Domain Stone.
magic_costs.minor_effect: A flicker in nearby Flame rites.
magic_costs.severe_effect: Renewal-channel scarring and ash-echoes near the overcharge site.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Cease overcharge, purify relics, restore disciplined sacrifice.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Catastrophic metaphysical breach if strain compounds.

government.government_type: Theocratic-martial council with flame-legitimacy as the source of authority.
government.ruling_body: The Ember Council, presided over by the senior Phoenix-Sworn.
government.religious_authority: Dawnfire Mystics and the Phoenix-Sworn interpret flame doctrine.
government.military_authority: The High Warmarshal; in practice Kael's Sunbreaker bloc holds field initiative.
government.economic_authority: The Forgekeeper guild controls Sunstone and sacred arms.
government.magical_authority: Dawnfire Mystics certify flame legitimacy and police forbidden rites.
government.succession_or_selection_method: Council seats earned through demonstrated, witnessed sacrifice; the senior Phoenix-Sworn is acclaimed, not inherited.
government.legitimacy_source: Truthfully borne cost and the unbroken burning of the Eternal Flame.
known_cracks_in_legitimacy: Kael's victories outshine the Council's caution
Hidden overcharge corruption undermines doctrinal authority
emergency_powers: Council suspension of overcharge bans during sieges
corruption_vulnerabilities: Investigations delayed when military morale depends on the accused

class_structure.description: The living embodiment of sacrifice; oath-bound flame leaders.
burdens: Expected to bear the greatest costs
class_structure.military_obligation: Lead from the front; rally rites.
class_structure.economic_role: Stipended by the Spire; forbidden personal wealth.
common_grievances: Spent by Kael's bloc as symbols

class_structure.description: Guild masters of Sunstone and sacred arms.
common_grievances: Excluded from flame legitimacy despite wealth

class_structure.description: Soldiers, forge-laborers, hearth-keepers, and the conscripted many.
class_structure.magic_access: Minor hearth and forge flame only.
common_grievances: Their dead become songs, not policy

trade_routes: Sunstone caravans from the eastern mines
economy.wartime_economy_behavior: Forge guilds donate arms during existential threats but quietly raise prices on overcharge relics the Council bans.
famine_or_shortage_risks: Eastern Sunstone mines overrun by Abyss
economy.keeper_attack_vector: Engineer healing-sap scarcity so Radiance turns to unsafe artificial healing and overcharge doctrine.

military_doctrine.strategic_identity: Hold the line, shield civilians, and burn corruption before it spreads.
military_doctrine.defensive_strategy: Layered flame-walls and shieldwalls that trade ground slowly while evacuating civilians.
military_doctrine.offensive_strategy: Decisive cleansing strikes on corruption nodes, then withdraw before overextension.
military_doctrine.logistics_strategy: Forge-town relays and Sunstone caravans; vulnerable to sap and food shortages.
military_doctrine.intelligence_strategy: Flame-witness scouts and pilgrim networks; weak against Abyss ledger espionage.
military_doctrine.keeper_exploit: Bait Radiance into spectacular last stands that spend its heroes and its Flame.
military_doctrine.void_escalation: Offer overcharge victories that win the battle and lose the renewal.

preferred_deescalation_methods: Honorable ceasefires that preserve the living
warfront_behavior.negotiation_style: Blunt and honor-bound; values demonstrated cost over clever words.
warfront_behavior.occupation_style: Garrison-and-rebuild; tries to restore order but risks purge overreach.
warfront_behavior.resistance_style: Stubborn shieldwalls and martyr stands; hard to break, easy to bait.

major_locations.name: The Ember Spire
major_locations.location_type: Capital sanctum and seat of government
major_locations.description: A basalt-and-gold tower crowning the Eternal Flame, ringed by seminaries and forge-halls.
major_locations.political_function: Seat of the Ember Council and the Phoenix-Sworn.
major_locations.magical_function: Anchor of the Eternal Flame and flame-legitimacy rites.
major_locations.military_function: Command of the vanguard and the Radiant Guard.
major_locations.spiritual_function: Heart of Ashfall Remembrance and Phoenix Vigil.
known_secrets: The Council quietly debates overcharge bans
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Let Kael's glory erode Council authority until overcharge bans collapse.
void_symptoms: A faint second voice in the Flame during Vigil
quest_hooks: Investigate why consecrations near the Spire are failing

major_locations.name: Cinderwatch
major_locations.location_type: Frontier fortress town facing the Abyss east
major_locations.description: A soot-stained wall-town guarding the Sunstone mines and the road to the soul-harvest frontier.
major_locations.political_function: Forward command of the eastern warfront.
major_locations.economic_function: Sunstone mining and forward arms depot.
major_locations.military_function: Anchor of the eastern defense line.
major_locations.spiritual_function: Frontline cremation and oath-taking for new soldiers.
major_locations.civilian_function: Refuge for frontier families and miners.
contested_by: Ashen Martyrs (for doctrine of its garrison)
known_secrets: Overcharge relics are field-tested here against Council ban
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Bait the garrison into martyr charges that feed Abyss harvest engines.
void_symptoms: Heat without warmth after overcharge tests
quest_hooks: Decide whether to expose Cinderwatch's overcharge tests

culture.daily_life_summary: Life is ordered by the forge bell and the Flame's hours; work is hard, honor is public, and grief is communal.
culture.family_customs: Households keep a hearth-ember from the Spire; oaths and trades pass parent to child.
culture.love_and_marriage_customs: Betrothals are sealed at a shared hearth; partners exchange a willingly given burn-scar as a vow of shared cost.
culture.education_system: Forge apprenticeship and seminary catechism; children learn the songs of the honored dead before letters.
culture.work_and_apprenticeship: Apprentices bind to a master for seven years; debt-binding is common and resented.
culture.food_and_market_life: Ash-baked bread, smoked frontier meats, and imported sap-teas; markets cluster around forge-squares.
culture.funeral_or_death_customs: Sacred cremation; the living take up an oath from the dead so renewal follows mourning.
public_honors: The Ember Mark for disciplined sacrifice
taboos: Claiming credit you did not pay for
common_sayings: The flame remembers what you gave, not what you claimed.
A clean flame needs no audience.
children_common_beliefs: The Flame can hear a lie
An ember from home keeps bad dreams away
Heroes are reborn in the morning sun
class_differences: Sworn forbidden wealth; Forgekeepers rich but unhallowed
Emberfolk praised in song, spent in policy

religion.central_belief: Willing sacrifice transforms loss into renewal, and the Eternal Flame remembers what is freely given.
sacred_symbols: The eight-rayed Sun of the Flame
common_prayers_or_oaths: By what I give, not what I take.
Let me be a clean flame.
heresies: The Martyr's Creed (death as the highest rite)
religion.relationship_to_death: Death is a passage to be kept clean; the dead are honored by oaths taken up, not by being spent again.
religion.relationship_to_sacrifice: Sacrifice is sacred only when willing, limited, and protective.
religion.relationship_to_memory: Memory is carried as inherited oaths; forgetting the cost is the true dishonor.
religion.relationship_to_truth: Hidden cost is the deepest lie; a clean flame is an honest one.
religion.keeper_corruption_strategy: Promote the Martyr's Creed and the Unlimited Flame heresies as truer devotion.
religion.void_false_revelation_style: A radiant vision promising that brighter burning is holier burning.

factions.name: Ember Council
factions.short_doctrine: Disciplined, limited sacrifice under flame legitimacy.
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Caution read as weakness amid existential war.
factions.player_use: Patron for lawful, disciplined paths and overcharge bans.

factions.name: Dawnfire Mystics
factions.short_doctrine: Guardians of clean flame and soul-flow; police forbidden rites.
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Can be marginalized as scolds when crowds want miracles.
factions.player_use: Allies for soul-flow healing and exposing overcharge corruption.

factions.name: Sunbreaker War Doctrine
factions.short_doctrine: Maximal output to win the existential war by any flame necessary.
factions.player_use: Powerful but corrupting patron for aggressive paths.

factions.name: Forgekeeper Guild
factions.short_doctrine: Control Sunstone and arms; prosperity through sacred craft.
factions.power_base: Economic control of Sunstone and weapons.
factions.player_use: Source of arms, relics, and morally grey deals.

factions.name: Ashen Martyrs
factions.short_doctrine: Death freely sought is the purest devotion.
factions.player_use: Fanatical edge faction; recruiter of the grieving; villain or tragic ally.

factions.name: Radiant Guard
factions.short_doctrine: Protect civilians and the Spire; the shield of Radiance.
factions.keeper_vulnerability: Can slide from protection into purge zealotry.
factions.player_use: Law-and-order allies; gatekeepers of the Spire.

external_relations.hidden_relationship: Mutual dependency soured by fear of Radiance fire.
external_relations.primary_conflict: Radiance cleansing-fire used near groves without tree consent.
external_relations.primary_dependency: Radiance needs Verdance healing sap; Verdance needs Radiance to hold the Abyss line.
external_relations.resource_leverage: Verdance can embargo healing sap; Radiance can withhold frontier protection.
external_relations.magic_tension: Fire versus cycle: purification versus restoration.
external_relations.military_tension: Radiance burns corruption Verdance would rather cleanse slowly.
external_relations.historical_wound: A grove burned without consent during a past corruption scare.
external_relations.possible_alliance_condition: A shared Abyss soul-harvest threat on the border.
external_relations.keeper_exploit: Engineer a containment burn that creates medical scarcity and mistrust.
external_relations.void_exploit: Whisper to both that the other's method is desecration.

external_relations.hidden_relationship: Allies wary of each other's zeal.
external_relations.primary_conflict: Sanctuary fears Radiance purge overreach near refugees.
external_relations.primary_dependency: Joint anti-Abyss operations and market access.
external_relations.resource_leverage: Sanctuary controls Ember Road markets; Radiance provides flame-support.
external_relations.magic_tension: Radiance fire versus Sanctuary's accountable protection.
external_relations.historical_wound: A purge near a refugee shelter that Sanctuary never forgot.
external_relations.possible_break_condition: Radiance flame harms civilians under Sanctuary protection.
external_relations.keeper_exploit: Use proof of Radiance overcharge to stall a joint operation.
external_relations.void_exploit: Frame Radiance restraint as cowardice to Sanctuary hardliners.

external_relations.hidden_relationship: Pragmatic trade partners who distrust each other's values.
external_relations.primary_conflict: Radiance discipline versus Tempest's prized freedom.
external_relations.primary_dependency: Radiance needs Tempest sky-freight; Tempest wants Sunstone arms.
external_relations.resource_leverage: Tempest corsairs can blockade sky-lifts; Radiance can deny sacred arms.
external_relations.magic_tension: Oath-bound flame versus chosen-bond storm magic.
external_relations.military_tension: Tempest sees Radiance conscription as tyranny.
external_relations.historical_wound: A corsair crew burned for smuggling overcharge relics.
external_relations.possible_break_condition: Radiance forcing service on a free Tempest crew.
external_relations.keeper_exploit: Turn a smuggling incident into a freedom-versus-order war.

external_relations.primary_dependency: None overt; Abyss feeds on Radiance's wasted heroes.
external_relations.resource_leverage: Abyss counterfeits and corrupts captured Sunstone relics.

external_relations.possible_break_condition: Ceasefires always break when honored dead are desecrated.
external_relations.keeper_exploit: Bait martyr charges that feed the harvest engines.
external_relations.void_exploit: Promise Radiance heroes that overcharge can outburn the harvest.

internal_power_struggles.title: The Overcharge Ban
internal_power_struggles.issue: Whether high-output overcharge relics may be fielded against the Abyss.
internal_power_struggles.public_argument: Kael: 'Discipline is a luxury the dying frontier cannot afford.' The Council: 'A Flame spent in spectacle cannot renew us.'
internal_power_struggles.hidden_argument: Forgekeepers profit from overcharge; the Council fears losing legitimacy to Kael's victories.
possible_player_sides: Uphold the ban with the Mystics
internal_power_struggles.keeper_best_outcome: The ban collapses quietly and overcharge becomes doctrine.
internal_power_struggles.void_best_outcome: Overcharge spreads, deferring costs into the Flame.
internal_power_struggles.peaceful_resolution: Supervised, time-limited overcharge with Mystic oversight and public accounting.
internal_power_struggles.violent_resolution: A frontier mutiny fields banned relics and forces the Council's hand.
internal_power_struggles.third_order_effect: Young acolytes imitate overcharge rites; the renewal channel strains.
internal_power_struggles.fifth_order_effect: The Keeper gains as Radiance's sacrifice culture mutates toward spectacle and Void dependency.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player publicly credits the saved instead of themselves
if_then_because_examples.because: A clean flame needs no audience, and crediting others proves the cost was for them.

if_then_because_examples.if: A Forgekeeper is exposed selling banned overcharge relics
if_then_because_examples.then: Council suspicion of the whole guild rises
if_then_because_examples.because: Profiting from deferred cost endangers the Flame all Radiance depends on.

if_then_because_examples.if: A Tempest crew is forced into Radiance service during a crisis
if_then_because_examples.then: Tempest relations sharply worsen even if lives are saved
if_then_because_examples.because: Radiance forcing loyalty violates the very chosen-cost principle it claims to honor.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player submits to ritual review after a forbidden act
if_then_because_examples.then: Forgiveness becomes possible and a renewing path opens
if_then_because_examples.because: Radiance forgives truthfully borne cost more readily than concealment.

if_then_because_examples.if: A rival domain helps cleanse a Radiance ash-echo wound
if_then_because_examples.then: A conditional alliance can form despite old grievances
if_then_because_examples.because: Protecting clean death-passage is sacred enough to outweigh history.

starting_bonuses: Reputation for borne cost among Emberfolk
starting_burdens: Expectation to lead from the front
starting_faction_assumptions: Presumed loyal to the Ember Council
common_npc_reactions: Respect if you bear cost openly
Suspicion if you hide your methods
Hope projected onto you by the young
starting_rumors: 'The Sworn-blooded newcomer who credits the saved'
'Carries an oath too heavy for their years'
unique_origin_questions: Whose oath did you inherit, and is it finished?
Have you ever wanted to be martyred?
Do you credit the saved, or the saving?
possible_dark_secret_options: You once accepted a Void overcharge to win
You let a healer die to keep a charge going

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player destroys an Abyss soul-harvest engine with Void-amplified Radiance flame.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Radiance sees a heroic rescue achieved through corrupted amplification that bypassed sacrificial discipline.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Ashen Martyrs praise it; Dawnfire Mystics are alarmed; Forgekeepers want the overcharge data.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The engine is destroyed and captives survive.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Captives saved; Radiance reputation +15; Abyss local control -10; player Void resonance +4.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Young acolytes idolize the feat; Mystics open an inquiry into the flame's residue.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Acolytes imitate dangerous flame rites; a rumor spreads that the Phoenix's old limits are obsolete.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Kael's bloc pushes high-output relic doctrine; Sanctuary hesitates to accept Radiance flame support.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper benefits as Radiance's sacrifice culture mutates toward spectacle, Void dependency, and interdomain mistrust.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: +1 Keeper pressure now, +3 possible if overcharge doctrine is adopted.
cause_effect_examples.void_gain: A Void echo begins learning to wear the player's fire.
player_intervention_options: Publicly acknowledge the danger
Submit the relic for purification
Credit the captives, not the spectacle
Help Mystics define safe limits
Expose the Void residue before Forgekeepers replicate it

cause_effect_examples.root_event: A field healer, Liora, dies holding the medical tent open during an ashfall the player's unit advanced through.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Radiance honors her sacrifice but asks whether command spent the wounded like arrows.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Ashfall chaplains mourn; a Sworn demands an inquiry; Sunbreaker officers call it the cost of victory.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The wounded she shielded survive; the unit advances.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Healing capacity drops; soldiers begin calling the player 'the one she trusted.'
cause_effect_examples.second_order: A forge-master refuses work for three days in grief; morale wavers.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: A rumor begins that command spent healers like arrows.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: An inquiry pressures the Council over frontier spectacle doctrine.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: If unaddressed, martyr-hunger rises among the grieving and the soul-flow wound spreads.
player_intervention_options: Demand an honest inquiry
Take up Liora's oath publicly
Fund a sap shipment to replace lost healing
Protect her name from martyr-cult misuse

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player exposes Cinderwatch's secret overcharge relic tests, defying the Council ban.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Radiance is split between honoring truth and fearing the blow to frontier morale.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Dawnfire Mystics vindicated; Sunbreakers enraged; Forgekeepers scramble to bury evidence.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The tests are documented and made public.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Council suspicion of Forgekeepers +15; frontier morale -8.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Kael's authority is dented; a Forgekeeper patron seeks leverage against the player.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Banned relics are recalled, but a black market for them forms.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: The overcharge ban is reaffirmed with supervision, slowing frontier offensives.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Flame's renewal channel stabilizes slightly, denying the Keeper a quiet win.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Reduced — unless the morale drop triggers a desperate martyr offensive.
player_intervention_options: Offer a supervised compromise
Shield whistleblowers from reprisal
Help retune relics to safe output
Negotiate morale support for the frontier

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player burns a corruption-touched grove on the Verdance border to stop a spreading rot.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Radiance sees disciplined containment if the fire was controlled.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Radiant Guard praises decisiveness; Dawnfire Mystics ask whether the fire was sacred or merely military; Verdance mourns.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Rot contained; Radiance frontier safety +6; Verdance grief and suspicion rise.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Verdance restricts healing-sap exports to Radiance.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Radiance wounded resent Verdance; Forgekeepers push artificial healing devices.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Dawnfire Mystics warn of Stone strain from unsafe healing magic.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper benefits from interdomain resentment, medical scarcity, and technological overreach.
player_intervention_options: Seek tree consent or a Verdance witness first
Cleanse residue after the burn
Name the act emergency-only and apologize
Broker a sap-for-protection accord

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player refuses a glorious last-stand martyr charge and orders an honorable withdrawal that saves a cohort.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Radiance is divided: Mystics and renewalists approve; martyr-zealots cry cowardice.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Dawnfire Mystics praise discipline; Ashen Martyrs brand the player a coward; the saved soldiers are loyal for life.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The cohort survives; the position is lost.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Cohort loyalty +20; Ashen Martyr hostility +12; a cowardice rumor begins.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Honorable factions defend the player; the saved soldiers spread a counter-story.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Martyr doctrine loses some ground among the young who see survivors lead.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Frontier doctrine debate shifts toward preserving the living.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper loses ground as renewal culture is publicly reaffirmed.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Reduced, unless the lost position causes a worse defeat later.
player_intervention_options: Publicly own the choice and its cost
Counter the cowardice rumor with witnesses
Honor those who wanted to charge without indulging the creed
Retake the position later with a disciplined plan

metaphysical: Does Phoenix rebirth draw from the Eternal Flame, the Radiance Stone fragment, or accumulated oaths — or all three?
Can a scarred renewal channel ever fully heal?
political: Can the Ember Council survive Kael's prestige without either co-opting or purging him?
Who certifies flame legitimacy if the Mystics and Council disagree?
magic: What is the exact threshold where disciplined sacrifice becomes overcharge?
Can overcharge relics be retuned to safe output, or are they inherently Void-tainted?
faction: Are the Ashen Martyrs a heresy to be healed or an enemy to be fought?
How deep is Forgekeeper influence over arms policy?
npc: Is Kael a tragic patriot, a glory-addict, or a Void-tempted vessel — and can the player change which?
Which grieving NPCs can be pulled back from martyr addiction?
war_economy: How long can Radiance fight without Verdance healing sap?
What happens to the economy if the eastern Sunstone mines fall?
implementation: Should overcharge be modeled as a magic-system instability stat, a Void temptation event, or both?
How is oath burden tracked across inherited oaths between characters?

locked_decisions: Radiance magic must always involve cost, discipline, sacrifice, or flame legitimacy.
Radiance corruption must never be generic darkness; it must distort sacrifice, renewal, honor, and sacred fire.
Radiance internal politics must respect the Phoenix / Kael / Forgekeeper / Mystic fracture.
Binding or harvesting the honored dead is the one violation Radiance cannot forgive.
Overcharge and Void-amplified flame must always defer a hidden cost into the Flame, oath burden, or soul-flow.
Honorable retreat that preserves the living for renewal is honored, not shamed.
